lines.text: Before she was a monster, Medusa was a young woman famous for one thing. Her beautiful hair.
Then the sea god Poseidon attacked her, inside the temple of the goddess Athena.
Athena was furious. But she didn't punish Poseidon. She punished Medusa.
Her hair became living snakes. And anyone who looked at her face turned to stone.
She hid at the edge of the world, surrounded by statues of the men who came for her.
Then a king sent a young man named Perseus to bring back her head. Lowkey, a death sentence.
But the gods had his back. A curved blade from Hermes. A polished bronze shield from Athena.
Winged sandals, a magic bag, and a helmet that made him invisible.
He found her asleep, and he never once looked at her. Only at her reflection in the shield.
One swing. And from her body sprang the winged horse, Pegasus.
Even dead, her eyes still worked. Perseus held the head up in front of the king... and the whole court turned to stone.
In the end he gave it to Athena, who set Medusa's face on her shield forever.
Today, many people don't see a monster. They see a survivor.
So, was Medusa the villain of this story... or its first victim?
